title: Feat global settings
description: Feat's settings for one machine and one user, as authored in ~/.config/feat/settings.yaml. The file is optional and every value has a default, so a machine that has written none is fully configured. These settings are global: there is no per-project override. This schema is a draft for editor support; feat doctor performs the semantic validation.

version.description: Settings schema version. This build understands 1 only. It is separate from the project file's version, because the two files are two compatibility surfaces.

duration.description: A Go duration such as "5s", "250ms", or "1m30s".

command.description: An external command as an argument vector. The first element is the program and is never templated; later elements may contain {placeholders}.
The program followed by its arguments.

review.description: External commands review opens. Feat renders no diffs itself in v0. They are settings rather than project configuration because they are your tools rather than a fact about a project — which the editor default has always said, by falling back to $EDITOR. Command arguments may contain {project_id}, {task_id}, {task_key}, {repository_id}, {repository_path}, {base_commit}, and {branch}.

diff.description: Compares a repository against its recorded base commit. Defaults to git diff {base_commit}.

editor.description: Opens a repository for editing. Defaults to $EDITOR with {repository_path}.

status.description: Shows a repository's Git status. Defaults to git status --short --branch.

notifications.description: Attention notifications. They are settings rather than project configuration because they are about the person at the keyboard and the desktop they are using.

idle_grace_period.description: How long idle waits before it is worth reporting. It is measured from the idle transition, and agent.claude.idle_grace_period — which stays in project configuration, because it is the provider's — decides when an ended turn becomes idle in the first place.

suppress_while_attached.description: Suppress notifications for a task the user is already attached to.

resources.description: Resource sampling. It is a setting rather than project configuration because one sample measures the whole machine, whatever project asked for it.

sample_interval.description: How often whole-machine and per-task resources are sampled. Sampling is observational and never blocks task creation.
